focus: Specify accuracy and cost improvements, and design a more trustworthy, reproducible measurement of real Gate 1 requests.
noveltyJustification: This iteration turns the prior result decomposition into accuracy diagnostics, a selectively gated serving experiment, a real-request evaluation design, prompt-safe reproducibility fields, and per-path latency evidence.
keyQuestions: Which changes can raise accuracy or lower cost without weakening the route?
How can a new measurement better represent real Gate 1 requests and produce trustworthy estimates?
answeredQuestions: Which changes can raise accuracy or lower cost without weakening the route?
How can a new measurement better represent real Gate 1 requests and produce trustworthy estimates?

keyFindings.title: Improve accuracy by separating candidate recall, track choice, and abstention
keyFindings.summary: The Jev arm chooses among 16 track descriptions plus none; the keep statistic scores only exact final track match, while the secondary paraphrase probe scored Jev 2/14 and ripgrep 8/14. First measure candidate-set recall, then top-1, per-track confusion, and none/multi-track handling. Contrastive profiles and aliases are testable proposals, not measured improvements.

keyFindings.title: Put a calibrated selective path between the lexical baseline and Jev
keyFindings.summary: A production experiment could retain high-confidence lexical routing, invoke Jev only on ambiguous requests, and fall back to broad retrieval unless a threshold is validated. This could cut calls without narrowing on unsupported confidence; the current measurements do not establish safe thresholds.

keyFindings.title: The three-order protocol is evaluation repetition, not a proven serving requirement
keyFindings.summary: The existing call log has 768 test choices, 42 scored-probe choices, and one auth check. One choice instead of three would use roughly one third the test-choice calls per request, but cost savings, token reduction from shorter profiles, and accuracy changes were not measured. The run estimates 905,891 input tokens; dollar cost was excluded.

keyFindings.title: Build a request holdout with independently adjudicated labels
keyFindings.summary: Packet-description questions and the inverse paraphrase result indicate transfer risk. Collect a consented redacted sample of real routing requests with independently adjudicated intended tracks, explicit none and cross-track labels, then freeze source/time-separated holdout data before tuning. Report per-track metrics, coverage, abstention, confusion, and paired confidence intervals.

keyFindings.title: Keep prompts private while making the run reproducible
keyFindings.summary: Call rows include option order, attempt, result, probabilities, model/provider/version, and wall time, but not the question or a prompt digest. Avoid raw prompts by default; add a protected digest, corpus snapshot, prompt/option hashes, scorer commit, CLI/model version, and explicit retry/timeout outcome.

keyFindings.title: The aggregate timing is not live-request latency
keyFindings.summary: Nearest-rank computation from calls.jsonl gives test-choice p50/p95 330/390 ms, probe-choice 315/370 ms, and the single auth check 438 ms; report aggregate p95 is 391 ms. It mixes workloads and measures Jev calls, not end-to-end hook-to-search. Capture cold/warm full-path timing, counts, and percentile method.
